channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

item.title: Nature Communications: Targeting chemotherapy-induced CD200 via a nucleoside-enhanced nanocarrier for cancer immunochemotherapy
item.description: The efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade therapy is limited by the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Here this group identifies the chemotherapy-induced CD200 upregulation as a resistance mechanism then develops a nanotechnology-based framework for spatially selective CD200 silencing, thereby reprogramming TME and enhancing antitumor efficacy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bacterial whole-cell biosensors uncover spatially variable sialic acid availability within the inflamed mammalian gut
item.description: An engineered E. coli biosensor reveals in situ sialic acid bioavailability in the inflamed mouse gut, revealing spatial decoupling between microbial and host inflammatory responses and supporting therapeutic evaluation of sialidase inhibition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nuclear factor I connects H3K27M to a targetable purine dependency in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
item.description: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma is an aggressive childhood cancer commonly driven by H3K27M with few treatment options. This study links H3K27M-driven chromatin remodelling to NFI-dependent purine metabolism, causing ATIC/PNP-mediated metabolic rewiring and ATIC-targetable tumour dependence.

item.title: Nature Communications: Choline kinase α promotes glycolysis and tumor growth by phosphorylating and activating enolase 1
item.description: Tumor cells rely on increased glycolysis for growth. Here, authors show that choline kinase α activates enolase 1 through phosphorylation, promoting glycolysis and tumor progression in glioblastoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plant protoplasts display phytopodia
item.description: Plant cells are encased in cell walls that when digested leave spherical protoplasts. Here the authors report long, thin membrane protrusions from protoplasts termed phytopodia and discuss their potential role in the probing behaviour of the cell cortex.

item.title: Nature Communications: A bacteriocin from the commensal Streptococcus mitis prevents influenza infection-driven pneumococcal lung dissemination
item.description: Here, the authors show that a specific strain of commensal Streptococcus mitis bacteria, and its bacteriocins, reduce S. pneumoniae asymptomatic colonization and lung dissemination after influenza infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: A noncanonical reducing-domain architecture defines a distinct class of modular polyketide synthases
item.description: Colibactin is a microbiome-derived genotoxin linked to colorectal cancer. Here the authors use cryo-EM to reveal a distinct configuration of the polyketide synthase module of its biosynthetic enzyme ClbB, and show that it is widespread across diverse bacteria.

item.title: Nature Communications: A long-read based haplotype panel enhances imputation and discovery of functional small and structural variants
item.description: Here, the authors integrate long-read sequencing and statistical phasing to create the Han-SV panel, a comprehensive haplotype reference resource comprising 32.6 million SNVs, 3.2 million indels, and 172,569 structural variants from 943 Han Chinese individuals.

item.title: Nature Communications: Development and clinical validation of a multimodal AI framework to predict persistent fever during antibiotic therapy in hospitalized patients with cancer
item.description: Pucher et al. show that multimodal AI can predict whether fever will persist in hospitalized cancer patients 48 hours after starting antibiotics, potentially supporting risk stratification and targeted clinical decisions at this reassessment point.

Nature Communications: Atomic-resolution insights into interactions of rifampicin and rifamycin derivatives with orphan CYP143 of M. tuberculosis
item.description: The study reveals how the mutation associated with drug resistance facilitates the binding of rifampicin to the orphan enzyme of tubercular bacilli, thereby influencing protein-protein interactions. The findings explore pathogen adaptation mechanisms.

item.title: Nature Communications: An interaction module for mitochondrial ATP synthase assembly and maintenance in seed plants
item.description: Mitochondrial ATP synthase is crucial for cellular energy production, but how it is assembled and maintained in plants is not fully uncovered. Here, the authors show that MTF5 and MTF5P form an interaction module essential for ATP synthase assembly and maintenance in seed plants.

item.title: Nature Communications: Lithium coordination compound reduces nephrotoxicity and enhances therapeutic effects in Alzheimer’s disease female mice
item.description: Here authors rationally design a lithium coordination compound BuLiPro. Compared with conventional lithium carbonate, BuLiPro improves brain lithium bioavailability, enhances GSK-3β inhibitory potency and reduces nephrotoxicity. In female AD mouse models, BuLiPro mitigates tau and amyloid-β pathologies and rescues cognitive deficits, showing potential for safer lithium-based therapeutics.

item.title: Nature Communications: SMYD1 trimethylates myosin K129 to restrain cardiomyocyte hypercontractility
item.description: How the muscle-specific enzyme SMYD1 regulates heart contraction and contributes to inherited heart disease has remained unclear. Here, the authors show that SMYD1 modifies the motor protein myosin to restrain heart-cell contraction, linking loss of this activity to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

item.title: Nature Communications: A neuroimmune dichotomy for T cell immunity in the mesenteric iymph node in mice
item.description: The authors find that vagal and sympathetic neurons innervating the mesenteric lymph node sense distinct cytokines and release opposing signals—calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) and norepinephrine—to control the balance between regulatory and cytotoxic T cells during intestinal infection in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tomato NLR R1L mediates SlSPL3 degradation to trigger a growth-to-defense switch against Phytophthora infestans
item.description: Wang et al., characterize a tomato NLR protein R1L that specifically recognizes the Phytophthora infestans effector AVR1. The AVR1-R1L-SlSPL3-SlLTP3 module mediates a growth-immunity trade-off. In uninfected plants, SlSPL3 promotes growth and suppresses immunity via SlLTP3. Upon infection, R1L-mediated SlSPL3 degradation activates immunity and represses growth.

item.title: Nature Communications: A small RNA regulates iron homeostasis and host mucus colonization in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
item.description: Here, the authors show how the beneficial gut bacterium Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron adapts to the intestinal mucous layer, identifying a small RNA regulator that balances capsule production, iron uptake, and host glycan utilization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
item.description: Neural decoding is widely used to understand how the brain represents the world, but data leakage can distort the results. Here the authors show that data leakage from preprocessing and cross-validation can both inflate and deflate decoding accuracy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus
item.description: In this study, the authors show that seasonal live-attenuated influenza vaccination provides cross-protection against lethal infection with an antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 virus in ferrets, potentially through respiratory cellular immune responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Restoring global forest canopy structure complexity for potential local warming mitigation
item.description: Forest biophysical cooling is constrained by limited land for afforestation. This study suggest that increasing canopy structural complexity enhances forest biophysical cooling by 0.25 °C globally, offering a land-efficient forest management strategy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Iron supplementation in iron-deficient Kenyan infants: a randomised controlled trial of vaccine immunogenicity
item.description: In a trial of 288 Kenyan infants, daily iron supplements reduced iron-deficiency anaemia but did not improve antibody responses to routine vaccines. Diphtheria antibody levels were modestly lower with iron, while seroprotection rates were similar.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD300LD drives osteoclastogenesis and inflammatory bone loss by sensing cholesterol and activating FES SYK STAT3
item.description: Osteoclast overactivation causes inflammatory bone loss in periodontitis and arthritis. Here, the authors show that CD300LD drives osteoclastogenesis via a cholesterol-activated FES–SYK–STAT3 axis, and its deletion reduces bone loss and inflammation in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hepatokine AGP2 mediates physical exercise-induced bone augmentation through liver-bone signaling communication
item.description: Exercise helps maintain strong bones, but the signals linking physical activity to bone growth have remained unclear. Here, the authors show that in mice exercise stimulates the liver to release AGP2, a hormone-like protein that promotes bone formation and protects against bone loss, revealing a potential treatment strategy for osteoporosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: A wearable reconfigurable surface electrode network for spatiotemporal control of hand motor output
item.description: Selective non-invasive hand control remains challenging. Here, the authors present a wearable 32-electrode surface-stimulation system with programmable active–return routing, enabling current-path mapping and task-level control of wrist and hand actions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mechanistic insights into intracellular phase separation and maturation of FUS LC revealed by in-cell NMR
item.description: Nishida and colleagues use in-cell NMR to capture time-dependent changes associated with the formation and maturation of FUS protein droplets, highlighting the influence of the cellular environment on these processes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence
item.description: Adolescence is a period of heightened sensitivity to social experiences. Here, the authors show that unexpected social feedback shapes self-esteem most strongly in adolescence, both in the lab and in daily life.

item.title: Nature Communications: An explainable deep-learning framework for predicting multisystem outcomes in comorbidity-free MASLD
item.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects many organs, but long-term risks are hard to predict. Here, the authors show that in subset of MASLD patients indicated for biopsy, explainable AI uses liver biopsy images, clinical tests and yearly lifestyle data to predict multiple outcomes and plot changing risk over time.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diabetes subtyping without HbA1c enhances identification of severe insulin-deficient diabetes
item.description: Here, the authors propose a simplified diabetes subtyping approach that excludes HbA1c. The approach more accurately identifies severe insulin-deficient diabetes and improves prediction of beta-cell dysfunction and retinopathy in the tested cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: De novo identification of protein domains in cryo-electron tomography maps from AlphaFold2 models
item.description: Identifying proteins in medium- to low-resolution cryo-electron tomography density maps remains challenging. Here the authors develop DomainSeeker, which combines AlphaFold2 models with experimental data to identify protein domains from density maps.

item.title: Nature Communications: Subsets of regulatory T cells are CD1a-reactive and dysfunctional in psoriasis
item.description: T regulatory cells (Treg) cells may be involved with the regulation of immune responses in psoriasis. Here, using psoriasis samples from humans, the authors characterize the function of CD1a-responsive Treg cells in psoriasis and show that these cells secrete IL-10 in response to lysophosphatidylcholine and are found in close proximity to CD1a + antigen-presenting cells and are potentially dysfunctional in psoriasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bacteria-induced TLR2 signaling unleashes multiple mechanisms to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance cancer immunity
item.description: Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling is known to support T cell priming, but how different TLRs regulate intratumoral effector T cell function is unknown. The authors here demonstrate that TLR2 signaling in dendritic cells upon Listeria infection enhances cancer immunity by disrupting regulatory T cells and promoting tumor antigen presentation by DCs to CD8 T cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: A macrocyclic peptide inhibitor of the antibiotic transporter NorA
item.description: In this work, peptide efflux pump inhibitors were developed for Staphylococcus aureus NorA to serve as antibiotic adjuvants by leveraging chemical synthesis and design, structure-based insights, and screening approaches to probe NorA pocket engagement.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dissecting the root-fungal interface in 3D reveals spatially distinct signalling landscapes
item.description: Plant-fungal interactions in the rhizosphere influence plant health. Here the authors describe an optically transparent granular microgel matrix that mimics the mechanical properties of natural microenvironments to dissect fungal development and pathogenesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: A meta-analysis of genome-wide DNA methylation in endometriosis
item.description: Epigenetics are increasingly thought to have a role in endometriosis. Here, the authors meta-analyse DNA methylation data to show the methylation differences between healthy endometrial tissue and ectopic endometrial lesions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Iso-Seq enables discovery of novel isoform variants in human retina at single-cell resolution
item.description: Iso-Seq enabled isoform discovery of human retina at single cell levels. This study revealed novel isoforms, splice junctions and alternative promoters across major retinal cell types, providing insights into the retinal transcriptomic landscape.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD33-CD45 interaction in Alzheimer’s disease susceptibility
item.description: CD33 and CD45 are both genetically linked to Alzheimer’s risk. Here the authors show the two proteins physically interact, and this interaction is increased in Alzheimer’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Distinct mechanisms of CNV formation at the human 15q13.3 locus
item.description: Recurrent copy-number variants at chromosome 15q13.3 cause neurodevelopmental disorders. Using long-read genome assemblies the authors show that these events arise via recombination promoted by inversions that vary in frequency across populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: EcoVAE: a generative deep learning method for global species distribution prediction
item.description: Predicting where species live is key to protecting biodiversity. The authors present EcoVAE, a generative model that rapidly and accurately predicts global species distributions, reveals species associations, and identifies sampling gaps.

item.title: Nature Communications: Host control of rhizobial proliferation in soybean nodules
item.description: Legumes must tightly regulate rhizobial proliferation to optimize symbiotic benefits and avoid pathogenicity. Here the authors show a role for cell wall derived demethylesterified pectin in constrains rhizobial growth in soybean nodules

item.title: Nature Communications: Autosomal dosage compensation in aneuploidy and cancer involves transcriptional burst regulation
item.description: Aneuploidy alters chromosome copy number and is often associated with impaired cellular function. Here, the authors show that cells compensate for autosomal chromosome gains and losses through genome‑wide transcriptional and protein‑level buffering mechanisms, helping to maintain gene dosage balance in normal and cancer cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-molecule landscape of DNA replication pausing
item.description: Rare DNA replication pauses can destabilise genomes but are hard to detect. Here, the authors use single-molecule nanopore sequencing to map pauses across a eukaryotic genome. They find widespread pauses enriched near transcribed genes and with a leading-strand bias over the promoter of an epigenetically regulated gene.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bidirectional control of a metabolic transition by the GID ubiquitin ligase
item.description: This study characterizes the regulation, specificity, and functions of the Gid11 substrate receptor of the GID/CTLH ubiquitin ligase in budding yeast, revealing a role for Gid11 in metabolic control during the glucose-to-ethanol transition.

item.title: Nature Communications: 3D-MINSTED nanoscopy and protein tracking in densely labelled living cells
item.description: 3D-MINSTED enables single fluorophore 3D tracking with precision down to <1 nm. Despite dense labelling and background, it resolves sub-10 nm DNA-origami spacing and 16 nm kinesin-1 steps in fixed and living cells at high labelling density.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
item.description: Here the authors report a link between the gut microbial metabolite PAGln and aortic aneurysm and dissection in patients and show that it worsens disease in mice by promoting inflammation in the aortic wall.

item.title: Nature Communications: ORE1 stabilizes PIF4 protein through a UBP12/UBP13-dependent regulatory module in thermomorphogenesis
item.description: Plants adapt their growth to warmth, but how aging signals tune protein stability remains unclear. Here, the authors show that the senescence factor ORE1 acts as a scaffold to stabilize the heat regulator PIF4 via UBP12/UBP13-mediated deubiquitination, driving warmth induced growth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Longitudinal changes in mis-splicing in a cohort of female twins are widespread and highlight mechanisms of ageing
item.description: This study identifies a striking increase in alternative splicing errors in ageing female twins over a six-eight-year timespan, providing insights into the molecular mechanisms of both healthy ageing and age-related diseases.

item.title: Nature Communications: A multimodal ultrasound foundation model for diagnosis of unexplained lymphadenopathy
item.description: Unexplained lymphadenopathy (ULA) has the potential to delay cancer diagnosis due to its complex nature, and the current ultrasound artificial intelligence models that rely on single-modality static images can be limited in their clinical applicability. Here, the authors show that the ultrasound multimodal foundation model LSF-NET could improve diagnosis of ULA.

item.title: Nature Communications: Biomass-based platform for pesticide management balancing field efficacy with postharvest residue via dynamic adhesion switch
item.description: Pesticide formulations must balance two competing requirements—robust adhesion during cultivation and efficient removal in postharvest. Here, the authors developed a thermoresponsive biomass-based dynamic adhesion switch and constructed a Pickering emulsion system loaded with the UV-sensitive pesticide emamectin benzoate.

item.title: Nature Communications: Eco-evolutionary dynamics of active virus-host interactions in a freshwater lake revealed through metaHi-C
item.description: In this study, the authors detect phage-bacteria associations using metaHiC, revealing diverse community-level infection dynamics in freshwater including cellular level co-infection, broad host range and kill-the-winner; and link them to underlying evolutionary processes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Harnessing plant cells as oral drug delivery capsules for synergistic therapy of ulcerative colitis
item.description: Plant cells have been explored as carriers for drug delivery through genetic engineering. Here, the authors report a plant cell-based oral colon-targeted delivery system that links drug-loaded, maleimide-modified liposomes to carrot cells through maleimide-thiol click chemistry.

item.title: Nature Communications: CARM1-mediated methylation controls interactions of ALIX with key partners important for cytokinesis
item.description: ALIX methylation by CARM1 controls CD2AP levels at the midbody and is important for cytokinesis. Their findings reveal a role for protein arginine methylation in the last step of cell division.

item.title: Nature Communications: Immunoglobulin A promotes stable colonization of Bifidobacterium to protect against allergic inflammation under fiber deprivation
item.description: Here, the authors show that Bifidobacterium induces IgA that enhances its mucosal persistence under fiber-deprived conditions, with its metabolites suppressing allergic inflammation, revealing a self-reinforcing host–microbial mutualism.

item.title: Nature Communications: A leptin receptor–LRP1 complex in the choroid plexus and tanycytes mediates leptin entry into the mouse brain
item.description: Leptin resistance in obesity may reflect impaired transport of leptin into the brain. Here, the authors show that an LRP1–LepR complex in the choroid plexus and tanycytes mediates leptin entry and is disrupted in obesity.

item.title: Nature Communications: A scalable pipeline for patient-matched pediatric solid tumor models and cell lines
item.description: An open-access collection of orthotopic patient-derived xenografts (O-PDXs) of pediatric solid tumours has previously been reported, representing an invaluable resource for preclinical research. Here, the authors expand this resource by generating 3D organoids, 2D primary cultures, and cell lines from these O-PDXs and demonstrate that these models preserve key molecular and cellular features of the original tumours.

item.title: Nature Communications: ALK R1275Q expands Schwann cell precursor-like cells during sympathoadrenal commitment, creating a permissive state for neuroblastoma initiation
item.description: Neuroblastoma develops from the sympathoadrenal lineage of the neural crest, with activating ALK mutations being frequent oncogenic events. Here, the authors develop a patient-derived iPSC model of sympathoadrenal development and find that the ALK activating mutation, R1275Q, drives expansion of Schwann cell precursor-like cells in early sympathoadrenal development establishing a permissive state for neuroblastoma initiation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatiotemporal brain dynamics of limb ownership perception
item.description: Using magnetoencephalography, the authors generate a time-resolved whole-brain map of neural activity underlying the experience that a hand is one’s own, revealing how distributed cortical and cerebellar networks are sequentially engaged.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ultralow-volume shallow microwell-based collection and processing for scalable spatial proteome mapping of tissues
item.description: Spatial proteome mapping is essential for understanding tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment. Here, authors report USMCP-MS, a robust, scalable, unbiased spatial proteomics method for proteome mapping of tissues at high spatial resolutions as well as high-throughput single voxel proteomics.

item.title: Nature Communications: A quantitative deep-learning-based framework reveals a continuum of chromatin sensitivities across transcription factors
item.description: The authors develop a deep-learning-based framework revealing that TF binding sensitivity to chromatin is a continuum rather than a binary feature, and that binding patterns can be explained by a mixture of hierarchical and cooperative mechanisms.

item.title: Nature Communications: Benzoxaboroles target CPSF3 for degradation through a SUMO-dependent pathway in trypanosomes
item.description: Benzoxaborole drugs, such as acoziborole, target CPSF3 and mRNA processing in multiple parasites. Here the authors find that these drugs rapidly and specifically target trypanosome CPSF3 for degradation, in a SUMO- and proteasome-dependent manner.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronically stable, frequency-selective auditory brainstem stimulation via ultra-flexible penetrating electrode arrays
item.description: Surface auditory brainstem implants have poor spatial resolution and limited tonotopic access. Here, the authors develop a high-density, ultra-flexible penetrating array for frequency-selective cochlear nucleus stimulation and use-dependent plasticity in downstream auditory circuits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
item.description: Here, the authors use super-resolution microscopy to show that desmin filaments extend beyond Z-lines and align with actin inside mouse skeletal muscle sarcomeres, where they help support force generation when sarcomeres are stretched.

item.title: Nature Communications: Super-resolution microscopy reveals distinct epigenetic states regulated by estrogen receptor activity
item.description: Here the authors show that super-resolution imaging reveals a spatial dimension to H3K27ac chromatin organization in ERα-responsive and endocrine-resistant breast cancer, linking elongated enhancer architectures with MED1 recruitment and enhanced transcription.

item.title: Nature Communications: Heparan sulfate sulfatases are essential for the patterning of human stem cell-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons
item.description: This study identifies the extracellular matrix modifying enzymes SULF1 and SULF2 as essential for human stem cells to acquire a midbrain dopaminergic neuron identity, the cell type selectively lost in Parkinson’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: The genetic and proteomic determinants of pediatric stature development and their link to adult height and type 2 diabetes
item.description: Childhood growth reflects complex genetic and biological processes, but their developmental timing is not fully understood. Here, the authors identify stage‑specific genetic and proteomic influences on growth from infancy through childhood, and reveal links between early growth patterns and later type 2 diabetes risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Foliar and floral frost damage reshape reproductive phenology with limited carry-over effects
item.description: Late spring frost can damage plant tissues and disrupt reproduction. The authors show that frost damage to leaves shortens the fruit development period, whereas damage to flowers prolongs it, with limited carry-over effects into the following year.

item.title: Nature Communications: Episodic memory consolidation by reactivation of human concept neurons during sleep reflects contents, not sequence of events
item.description: Recording from epilepsy patients during learning, recall, and sleep, the authors show that semantically tuned concept cells in the medial temporal lobe encode the content, but not the sequential order of remembered events

item.title: Nature Communications: A global atlas of digital dermatology to map innovation and disparities
item.description: The authors map 1.1 million dermatology images to assess the diversity of data used to train AI and find major gaps in darker skin tones and children, highlighting the importance of representation for future data collection.

item.title: Nature Communications: G3BP1-induced retrograde transport blockade triggers HSC activation and liver fibrosis via COPI alternative splicing
item.description: Liver fibrosis is driven by hepatic stellate cell activation, but its molecular drivers remain unclear. Here, the authors show that G3BP1 promotes COPI alternative splicing via SRPK1–hnRNPM, impairing Golgi-to-ER transport and causing ER stress that activates these cells and drives fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis for constitutive activation of oncogenic gp130 mutants found in human inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas
item.description: Inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas are benign liver tumors primarily driven by constitutively active gp130 mutants. The authors employ cryo-EM and mutagenesis to reveal the structural mechanism of ligand-independent activation of these mutants.

item.title: Nature Communications: Influenza A virus orchestrates ciliated cell fate and injury during the mucociliary damage repair cycle
item.description: In this study, the authors show how influenza A virus reshapes ciliated cell fate and function throughout the airway damage repair cycle, uncovering viral and host mechanisms that drive persistent mucociliary dysfunction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids
item.description: Tabernanthe iboga produces the medically important alkaloids voacangine and ibogaine, but key steps in their biosynthesis, as well as the biosynthetic route to the structurally distinct alkaloid ibophyllidine, have remained unresolved. Using genome sequencing, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and biochemical reconstitution, the authors identify the missing enzymes required for coronaridine and voacangine biosynthesis, elucidate the complete pathway to ibophyllidine, and achieve heterologous production of voacangine in Nicotiana benthamiana .

item.title: Nature Communications: Early-life skin molecular signatures are predictive of atopic dermatitis risk in an Asian preconception birth cohort
item.description: Here, via a multi-omics analysis of the infant skin microbiome and host immune markers, the authors identify preclinical molecular signatures in the first week of life that predict the onset of atopic dermatitis by 18 months, offering an early window for preventive care.

item.title: Nature Communications: Landscape fire sourced PM2.5, cause-specific paediatric hospitalisations, and the role of tree cover
item.description: Greater tree cover is associated with lower risks and burdens of landscape fire smoke-related hospitalisations in children and adolescents across seven countries and territories, suggesting potential benefits of expanding tree cover.

item.title: Nature Communications: Soybean Pb encodes a WD40 protein regulating pubescence tip morphology and seed size during domestication
item.description: The genetic basis of pubescence tip morphology remains poorly understood. Here, the authors identify a WD40 protein-encoding gene underlying trichome shape at the Pb locus and reveal potential links between trichome morphology, herbivory resistance, and seed size.

item.title: Nature Communications: Combinatorial mutagenesis of N-terminal sequences reveals expanded stability determinants of the Escherichia coli N-degron pathway
item.description: Understanding how a protein’s sequence impacts its stability is critical to modern protein science and engineering. Here, the authors screened over 2 million N-terminal motifs to understand what sequences lead to protein degradation via the N-degron pathway in the model microbe Escherichia coli .

item.title: Nature Communications: SMC5/6 safeguards chromatin compartments and TAD boundaries for genome stability
item.description: The SMC5/6 complex protects genome stability, but how it shapes 3D genome folding is unclear. Here, the authors show that SMC5/6 loss in human cells alters chromatin compartments and activates inflammatory and cancer-related genes, changes that are uncoupled from DNA damage.

item.title: Nature Communications: Wnk1 drives CD4+ T cell lineage fate determination and bone marrow homing in a mouse model of retinal autoimmune disease
item.description: CD4 T cells are central to the pathogenesis of uveitis and related inflammatory responses by promoting myeloid cell infiltration. Here, by leveraging scRNA-seq and a mouse model of experimental autoimmune uveitis, the authors identify the kinase Wnk1 as a key regulator of CD4 T cell differentiation, migration and metabolic reprogramming and as a coordinator of T cell-bone marrow crosstalk that contributes to myeloid-biased hematopoiesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: VHSeek: biology foundation model-based virus representations revealing virus host associations
item.description: The authors present VHSeek, a tool that uses DNA and protein sequence representations to predict viral hosts and prioritize candidate virus-host associations across large viral collections.

item.title: Nature Communications: Environmental toxicant-induced epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming of transposable elements
item.description: In this study, the authors, characterize how transposable elements respond to early-life toxicant exposures in adult mouse liver through epigenetic and transcriptional changes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Glycoverse: a multi-functional R framework for glycomics and glycoproteomics data analysis
item.description: Glyco-omics analysis is challenging because glycans have complex structures and analysis tools are fragmented. Here, the authors introduce glycoverse, an R toolkit that unifies glycan parsing, visualization, motif analysis and derived-trait analysis, and demonstrate its use in glycomics and glycoproteomics.

item.title: Nature Communications: A renewable autologous biomaterial for reprogramming cellular metabolism
item.description: Autologous blood-derived products are attractive materials for tissue repair. Here, the authors use gas-shearing microfluidics combined with ionic and fibrin-based enzymatic crosslinking to generate autologous serum microspheres, that improve joint lubrication and support cartilage repair in an osteoarthritis models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles
item.description: This study shows that arteriviruses, like coronaviruses, form pore complexes that span their double-membrane replication organelles, pointing to a conserved nidovirus strategy that links the synthesis, export and packaging of viral RNA.

item.title: Nature Communications: A genome-wide imaging screen reveals epigenetic and mechanistic partitioning of lamina-associated chromatin
item.description: Here the authors present a genome-wide imaging-based screen which identifies over 100 regulators of LAD positioning, revealing hnRNPK as a key organizer of nuclear architecture. The study uncovers that multiple mechanisms underlie the peripheral positioning of epigenetically distinct LAD subclasses and a genetic framework governing 3D genome organization and transcriptional regulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Viscoelasticity of synthetic antigen presenting cells reprograms T cell metabolism for TCR-T cell manufacturing and therapy
item.description: Li and colleagues have previously reported the generation of viscoelastic synthetic antibody-presenting cells for CAR-T therapy. Here the authors report that fast-relaxing synthetic viscoelastic activating cells presenting antigen promote the expansion of antigen-specific T cells toward a favourable metabolic state with enhanced anti-tumor efficacy in TCR-T cell therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: A protein repeat interruption rule governs Nebulin stability and explains in-frame NEB mutations
item.description: Nemaline myopathy is a congenital muscle disorder often caused by mutations in NEB, but how many in-frame deletions disrupt Nebulin function is unclear. Here, the authors show that partial super-repeat deletions destabilize Nebulin and cause severe disease phenotypes, whereas complete super-repeat deletions preserve protein function and muscle development.

item.title: Nature Communications: σ-complex stabilization shapes enzymatic C -glycosylation and restricts the scope of natural C -glycosides
item.description: Enzymes offer a sustainable route to C -glycosides, valuable compounds containing hydrolytically stable C-C bonds, but few are known to display C -glycosylation activity and their mechanism remains unclear. Here, the authors investigate a C -glycosyltransferase from maize, Zm UGT708A6, reveal two flexible gates that control substrate access and reactive conformations, and suggest that substrate hydroxylation patterns, protonation states, and σ-complex energetics restrict the scope of C -glycosides.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cholesterol dysregulation contributes to hematopoietic failure in parn -mutant zebrafish with implications for dyskeratosis congenita
item.description: Researchers show that abnormal cholesterol metabolism and Erk signalling disrupt blood formation in a zebrafish model of dyskeratosis congenita, identifying potential therapeutic targets for restoring healthy hematopoiesis in this patient population.

item.title: Nature Communications: ER-associated biogenesis of PINK1 preprotein for neuronal mitophagy
item.description: Neuronal mitochondria associate with Pink1 mRNA regulated by AMPK signalling. Here, the authors show, that the PINK1 protein switches between co- and post-translation import associated with ER chaperones depending on the localization of the mRNA.

item.title: Nature Communications: Local niche-derived immunosuppressive CXCR2 + cells impair antiviral immunity
item.description: The mechanisms underlying individual differences in the severity of viral infection remain to be explored. The authors here show in mice that differential brain accumulation of immunosuppressive CXCR2 + cells contributes to divergent disease outcomes and identify the skull bone marrow as a local source of these cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Linking human sources to antibiotic resistance genes in global surface waters
item.description: In this study, the authors used measurement data combined with modeling and machine learning to estimate global human generation of five individual ARGs and intI1 , discharge, and surface-water abundance, highlighting hotspots of per-capita generation and total abundance.

item.title: Nature Communications: var2csa transcription implicates variant surface antigen switching in cerebral malaria pathogenesis
item.description: In this study, the authors report case-control studies in Mali and Malawi showing that cerebral malaria is associated with increased transcription of var2csa and EPCR-ICAM1 dual binding PfEMP1s, rather than EPCR-binding variants alone suggesting that var gene regulation may be a driver of severe disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intravenous phage therapy for difficult-to-treat infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis of individual patient data
item.description: This systematic review synthesises evidence on clinical, microbiological and safety outcomes of intravenous phage therapy, together with pharmacokinetic and immune neutralisation data, suggesting therapeutic potential but raising questions about limitations of the intravenous route.

item.title: Nature Communications: A spectral framework for revealing the hidden low-dimensional structure in stochastic reaction networks
item.description: Stochastic reaction networks underline many noise-driven biological processes, but their high dimensionality makes it difficult to characterize transient dynamics and infer system properties from data. Here, the authors develop a stochastic Koopman operator-based spectral framework to identify dominant low-dimensional dynamical modes from simulated trajectories, enabling efficient analysis of moments, sensitivities, and cross-spectral densities, and demonstrate its utility for analyzing synthetic gene circuits, comparing intracellular controllers, and inferring initial-state distributions from time-resolved single-cell data.

item.title: Nature Communications: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations
item.description: Bischoff and colleagues present velotest, a statistical method for assessing RNA velocity visualisations, revealing substantial differences in how faithfully different methods, datasets and regions within a dataset represent underlying cellular dynamics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide association study identifies a functional myostatin variant increasing lean mass in humans
item.description: This large genome-wide meta-analysis identifies 63 genetic loci associated with lean mass, including a rare MSTN variant linked to greater muscle mass and strength, and provides insight into the long-term potential effects of myostatin inhibition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Benefits and harms of antihypertensive treatment a modelling study in 5.5 million electronic health records
item.description: A cardiovascular risk model was developed and externally validated in patients eligible for antihypertensive treatment. Findings suggest that antihypertensive treatment was more likely to prevent major cardiovascular events than cause serious falls.

item.title: Nature Communications: Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases drive cancer risk through subtype-specific and shared proteomic mediators
item.description: Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases (ENMs) may influence cancer development, but their effects across cancer trajectories remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that ENM subtypes are linked to cancer risk through shared and subtype-specific proteomic mediators.

item.title: Nature Communications: Expert operating skills learning-based intelligent shared control method for a CT-guided percutaneous biopsy robot
item.description: CT-guided lung biopsy requires precise needle placement while limiting radiation exposure and tissue injury. Here, the authors show that a robot using learned expert skills and shared control improves insertion stability, force regulation and targeting accuracy in phantom and animal tests.

item.title: Nature Communications: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
item.description: More redundancy doesn’t always mean more resilience. Here, the authors use seven-year-long metagenomics data from soils above Centralia’s coal seam fire to show that heat disturbance increases microbial functional redundancy but narrows environmental responsiveness, potentially lowering insurance against future stress.

item.title: Nature Communications: The evolutionary plateau of efflux-mediated drug resistance in mycobacteria
item.description: Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance in bacteria. Here, Sharma et al. use experimental evolution in mycobacteria and show that, after prolonged selection, drug resistance achieved through efflux pump overexpression reaches a stable level, apparently due to exhaustion of cellular energy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Early face-experience deprivation leads to long-lasting deficits in macaque cortical face processing
item.description: The emergence of category selectivity is not fully understood. Sharma and Livingstone show that when face experience is delayed in macaques, higher-order visual cortex remains plastic beyond early development, but the resulting neural representations do not develop typically.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vivo programming of dual-targeted CAR-T cells facilitates vascular disruption and T-cell infiltration in solid tumors
item.description: Li and colleagues introduce an mRNA lipid nanoparticle platform for the selective transfection of endogenous T cells within the spleen; by dual-targeted CAR T cell in vivo programming, the authors show that VEGFR2 CAR-T cells disrupt the tumor vasculature, favoring the infiltration and activity of tumor-directed CAR-T cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structure-guided design of a dual-antigen mRNA vaccine conferring broad protection against Henipaviruses
item.description: The authors develop a structure-guided mRNA vaccine combining two Nipah virus proteins. All vaccinated hamsters survive challenge with Nipah-Malaysia, Nipah-Bangladesh or Hendra virus, with reduced viral burden.

item.title: Nature Communications: Macrophage-exacerbated viral lung injury and mechanical overdistension-driven bacterial superinfection replicated in a human lung chip
item.description: Lung-on-a-chip methods can be used to characterize the function of various cells and biophysical cues within the lung microenvironment. Here, the authors use a lung-on-a-chip method to show that macrophages exacerbate viral lung injury and mechanical overdistention further promotes lung inflammation and bacterial superinfection, implicating SIRT1 as a candidate therapeutic target.

item.title: Nature Communications: A metal ion-assisted workflow for practical and scalable enrichment of small extracellular vesicles from biofluids
item.description: Efficient isolation of small extracellular vesicles is key for clinical applications. Here, the authors develop IonNet, a metal ion-assisted workflow that enables practical and scalable enrichment of functional small extracellular vesicles from biofluids via conventional centrifugation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes as saturated bioisosteres of meta -benzene
item.description: The authors synthesize bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes and provide support for their ability to mimic meta-substituted benzenes in biological contexts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Facial photographs reveal mortality risk beyond triage and clinical risk scores
item.description: Using 27,660 smartphone facial photos, researchers showed that the facial appearance from emergency admission predicts mortality and high-risk patients better than triage, early warning scores, vitals, or lab tests.

item.title: Nature Communications: Estimating malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa under intervention disruption using satellite-derived representations
item.description: Satellite-derived deep-learning-based environmental representations and Bayesian modelling suggest that malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa could reach 422 million annual cases under a low-intervention baseline.

item.title: Nature Communications: Parental leave benefits and fathers’ postpartum mental health in Sweden
item.description: Fathers receiving basic-level parental leave benefits were more likely to use any mental healthcare, be prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics or use specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related parental benefits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Impact of Comorbid Depression and Anxiety on the Mortality among Adults with Cardiometabolic Diseases
item.description: Cardiometabolic diseases often coexist with depression or anxiety, but their prognostic implications remain unclear. Here, the authors show that depression/anxiety after cardiometabolic disease onset is associated with higher mortality, with variation by socioeconomic status.

item.title: Nature Communications: Selective mTOR inhibition via FLCN drives TFE3-dependent VLDL-TG secretion and protects from MAFLD/MASH
item.description: The study identified a pathway that coordinates VLDL assembly and secretion regulated by non-canonical mTOR signaling. Targeting the pathway efficiently suppresses liver steatosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ikaros transcription factors prevent the activation of an endothelial cell program in bone marrow hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells
item.description: Taroni, Bianchi et al demonstrate that the Ikaros and Helios transcription factors restrict the plasticity of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells by preventing the activation of an endothelial cell program.

item.title: Nature Communications: RSM01, an extended half-life RSV monoclonal antibody with a high barrier to in vitro resistance
item.description: RSM01 showed broad neutralizing activity against circulating LMIC RSV strains. Authors found a high barrier to resistance, supporting RSM01 as an alternative should resistance emerge with widespread use of current licensed anti-RSV mAbs.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mpox virus replication and drug resistance in the central nervous system of a man with advanced human immunodeficiency virus at autopsy
item.description: This study provides insight into MPXV co-infection with HIV. Authors quantified MPXV DNA in 76 autopsy tissues, including visceral organs and brain. Authors recovered infectious MPXV from CNS tissues, and performed tissue sequencing, revealing widespread tecovirimat resistance-associated isolates.

item.title: Nature Communications: Atomic-level coordination-engineered quantum dots orchestrate mitochondrial energy rescue for diabetic bone regeneration
item.description: Here the authors identify deleterious mitochondrial transfer in osteoimmunological processes as a key driver of impaired diabetic bone healing and engineer quantum dots to boost energy-regulation and restore functional mitochondrial transfer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Partially functional hypomorphic missense variants in BRCA2 are reduced penetrance pathogenic variants
item.description: Germline BRCA2 reduced penetrance pathogenic missense variants partially reduce BRCA2 DNA repair activity, confer breast cancer lifetime risks of 25%, rarely cause homologous recombination deficiency in tumors and need modified clinical management.

item.title: Nature Communications: Forced displacement is associated with health service delivery disruption beyond the effects of armed conflict
item.description: Analyzing 193 countries over 24 years, researchers find that sudden mass displacement is linked to childhood vaccination coverage falling 3–6 percentage points for up to three years, independently of armed conflict or natural disasters.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mapping redox networks in cardiomyocytes reveals non-overlapping response pathways for cytosolic versus mitochondrial H₂O₂ signaling
item.description: The site of hydrogen peroxide production in heart muscle cells controls how the signal spreads, which proteins are oxidized, and whether redox signaling remains adaptive or disrupts sarcomeres and contraction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Site-specific N-glycoproteomic analysis of extracellular vesicles from seminal plasma reveals the molecular typing of azoospermia
item.description: This study presents EVGlyco, a low-input platform for site-specific N-glycoproteomic analysis of biofluid EVs. It identifies site-specific N-glycan signatures in seminal plasma EVs that distinguish azoospermia types and nonobstructive subtypes.

item.title: Nature Communications: TRIM47 drives cardiac ischemia/reperfusion injury by impairing mitochondrial function and fatty acid metabolism in male mice
item.description: Cardiac I/R injury is a prevalent and intractable clinical complication. Here, the authors show that TRIM47 facilitates ubiquitination-dependent nuclear translocation of FOXO1 and the subsequent inhibition of HNF4α, thereby aggravating mitochondrial dysfunction, FAO defects and cardiac I/R injury.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular profiling of repeated self-sampled blood reveals dynamic immune phenotypes in young adults
item.description: In this study, the authors used repeated at-home blood sampling to track changes in the immune-related protein during the recent pandemic. The study reveals shorter-lived shifts alongside stable proteins, providing insights missed by standard one-time blood tests

item.title: Nature Communications: Sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life and biological aging and age-related diseases
item.description: Exposure to sugar rationing during the first 1,000 days of life was associated with slower biological aging in adulthood, with stronger associations after longer exposure. It was also associated with lower risks of several age-related diseases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Post-pandemic immunity debt and environmental decoupling reshape urban influenza transmission
item.description: Using 1.88 million clinical records from Macau and regional and global surveillance, in this study, the authors show how reduced population immunity and renewed travel reshaped post-pandemic influenza transmission and weakened its usual links with climate.

item.title: Nature Communications: Co-administration of the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 vaccination is well-tolerated in immunosuppressed patients highly vulnerable to infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus: the results of the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled, RAPID-PROTECTION trial
item.description: In this clinical trial, authors found that administering the COVID-19 antibody AZD7442 before vaccination was safe in immunocompromised adults and boosted immune responses. The findings support combining antibodies and vaccines to protect vulnerable people.

item.title: Nature Communications: Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
item.description: Researchers developed UniRG, a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes clinically aligned composite rewards for medical imaging report generation. UniRG outperforms prior models and demonstrates strong generalization across unseen hospitals and datasets

item.title: Nature Communications: Topographical mismatch sustains open microchannels in living soft tissue for non-destructive protein biopsy
item.description: Skin-attached devices can easily inflame or collapse. Here, the authors show a multi-lobed microneedle device that holds micron-scale conduits open for seven days, allowing repeated protein sampling from interstitial fluid

item.title: Nature Communications: Pharmacological chaperone treatment with Cystadane in aspartylglucosaminuria: an open-label, phase Ib/II trial
item.description: Here, this phase Ib/II interventional clinical trial shows that betaine/Cystadane is safe to use and significantly reduces urinary accumulation of glycoasparagines and increases aspartylglucosaminidase activity in aspartylglucosaminuria.

item.title: Nature Communications: Toward personalized deep brain stimulation via white matter stimulation and microstructure in depression
item.description: A study of 51 patients receiving deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant depression shows that individual white matter stimulation and integrity jointly influence antidepressant response, supporting more personalized neuromodulation strategies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder revealed through predictive symptom networks
item.description: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder causes cyclical mental symptoms, but how these symptoms unfold over time is not yet understood. This study reveals temporal patterns and identifies anxiety as a promising treatment target.

item.title: Nature Communications: Prospective and genetic analyses implicate lower immunosurveillance in the aetiology of prostate cancer
item.description: Role of specific immune and inflammation-related pathways and protein markers in the development of prostate cancer remains to be elucidated. Here the authors show evidence for potential protective role of dendritic cell mediated immunosurveillance, with protective associations with immune and inflammation related proteins measured more than seven years before diagnosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: LLM ensemble PREVIA predicts future PTSD risk from emergency department trauma narratives with expert-level accuracy
item.description: PTSD screening is rarely feasible in busy emergency departments. Here, the authors show that a scalable AI ensemble can predict 1-month PTSD risk from a single routine-care question, a first step toward low-burden implementation at point of care.

item.title: Nature Communications: Calpain-mediated TBP cleavage disturbs neuronal AMOT-YAP1 signalling
item.description: TBP fragments activate calpains and disrupt AMOT-YAP1 signalling, revealing a pathway involved in normal neural development and implicated in spinocerebellar ataxia type 17.

item.title: Nature Communications: Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
item.description: A soft robotic and computational framework replicates left atrial hemodynamics. Validated with human and porcine data, the platform enables personalized preclinical testing of left atrial appendage occlusion devices for atrial fibrillation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Non-canonical FOXO1 signaling governs epithelial barrier integrity through spatial regulation of the E-cadherin–β-catenin complex
item.description: Bacterial challenge rapidly weakens epithelial barriers through a non-canonical, FOXO1–β-catenin–E-cadherin axis that disrupts adherens junctions and redistributes E-cadherin independently of transcription or proteolysis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Adipocyte enhancer binding protein 1 (AEBP1) inhibition mediates cardiac reverse remodeling by regulating MRTFB and RUNX2 signaling
item.description: Cardiac fibrosis contributes to adverse remodeling and heart failure progression, but its molecular drivers remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that ACLP/AEBP1 promotes cardiac fibrosis and AEBP1 inhibition following injury, improves cardiac structure and function.

item.title: Nature Communications: A pilot randomized controlled trial of medically tailored groceries and resource coaching: secondary and exploratory diet and health outcomes
item.description: Here, the authors report secondary and exploratory outcomes of a pilot randomized controlled trial exploring a food-is-medicine intervention of medically tailored groceries with or without resource coaching against usual pantry support. All groups improved over time in food security, diet quality, and perceived health, but baseline-adjusted analyses did not identify clear differences between the groups.

item.title: Nature Communications: A 17.2T MRI atlas and multiparametric exploration of the mouse hypothalamus reveal sexual dimorphism and lateralization
item.description: This 17.2 Tesla MRI study provides a nucleus-level atlas of the mouse hypothalamus, mapping its anatomy, structural and functional connectivity, and neurochemical profile, revealing sex-related differences in structure and neurochemistry.

item.title: Nature Communications: [ 18 F]FET PET enables histopathology-validated detection of non-contrast-enhancing glioblastoma
item.description: Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CE-MRI) is standard for patients with glioblastoma, but its ability to detect metabolically active tumours cells at the infiltrative edge is limited. Here, the authors present a prospective biopsy-validated study demonstrating that ¹⁸F-FET PET imaging can detect tumour tissue beyond that detected by CE-MRI in patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial
item.description: It is unclear whether adjunct intra-arterial Tenecteplase during thrombectomy improves clinical outcomes in patients with acute large vessel occlusion. Here, the authors show that adjunct intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy does not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial
item.description: Medium-vessel occlusion accounts for a substantial proportion of acute ischemic stroke cases, yet optimal reperfusion treatment strategies remain unclear for patients ineligible for mechanical endovascular thrombectomy. Here, the authors show that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increases reperfusion rates for medium-vessel occlusion with acceptable safety, although statistically-significant improvements in 90-day functional outcomes were not detected in this phase-2 randomized trial.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intra-arterial tenecteplase for acute basilar artery occlusion with sufficient recanalization after thrombectomy: the INSIST-IT randomized clinical trial
item.description: Acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is a life-threatening cause of stroke, and whether intra-arterial tenecteplase after successful recanalization leads to improved outcomes is unclear. This randomized trial by Chen and colleagues was stopped early for safety concerns and shows that adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase does not improve functional outcomes in acute BAO.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mannitol-stimulated Copeptin for diagnosing Arginine Vasopressin Deficiency: a randomized controlled proof of concept and a single-arm pilot study
item.description: Distinguishing arginine vasopressin deficiency from primary polydipsia can be difficult and current tests are challenging. Here, the authors show that mannitol-stimulated copeptin may offer a simple, rapid, safe and accurate diagnostic alternative.

item.title: Nature Communications: Personalized adjunctive phage therapy for difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections
item.description: In this prospective study, authors found that personalized adjunctive local phage therapy was feasible and well tolerated in difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections, with 9 of 11 evaluable patients achieving remission.

item.title: Nature Communications: Resident cardiac macrophage-like cells induced by an ILC2 cytokine cocktail confer cardioprotection through enhanced efferocytosis in a mouse model of myocardial infarction
item.description: Resident cardiac macrophages (RCM) contribute to cardiac repair after myocardial infarction (MI); however, their number is reduced upon injury. Here, the authors identify a population of efferocytosing CD301b+ macrophages that promote post-ischemic cardiac repair and develop an ex vivo protocol to generate RCM-like cells induced with enhanced efferocytic potential for post-MI cardioprotection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiscale neural dynamics reveal how striatal subregions shape stress vulnerability and resilience
item.description: This study shows that striatal subregions shape individual differences in stress vulnerability and resilience through distinct patterns of multiscale network dynamics during stress coping.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pathology-adapted peptide–oligonucleotide nanohybrid mitigates glucocorticoid-induced bone loss
item.description: Glucocorticoids can cause severe bone loss and osteonecrosis. Here, the authors develop a pathology-adapted peptide–oligonucleotide nanohybrid that delivers miR 26a-5p to mitigate bone loss and support vascular recovery.

item.title: Nature Communications: PRMT6 suppresses intestinal inflammation by epigenetically repressing IL-1β in mouse models of colitis
item.description: Epigenetic regulation in immune cells drive their physiological and pathologic development, including establishment of inflammatory states. Here the authors show in mouse colitis models, that genomic deletion of the protein arginine methyltransferase PRMT6 leads to a selective upregulation of IL-1β in macrophages and to exacerbated inflammation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Podocyte-derived palmitic acid drives p53 S-palmitoylation and CD103 + CD4 + T cell differentiation in humanized mouse model of systemic lupus erythematosus
item.description: CD103 + CD4 + T cells mediate renal tissue injury in lupus nephritis (LN). To date, the mechanism instructing pathogenic CD103 + CD4 + T cell differentiation remains elusive. Here, the authors show that LN-associated podocytes undergo fatty acid oxidation reprogramming and release palmitic acid, thereby promoting p53 S-palmitoylation and Runx3 transcription in CD4⁺ T cells, ultimately sustaining pathogenic CD103⁺ T cell differentiation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-ancestry genome-wide and transcriptome-wide association analyses identify new risk loci and genes for inflammatory bowel disease
item.description: Large-scale meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies and advanced transcriptome-wide association studies identify new inflammatory bowel disease risk variants and genes, including druggable targets with potential for therapeutic repurposing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gut microbiome of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder associates with clinical severity
item.description: Here, the authors show that gut microbes in children with autism vary with clinical severity, including reduced predicted GABAergic capacity, with sensory atypicalities showing the most associations, suggesting particular gut–brain relevance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mapping hippocampal subfield heterogeneity across neurological disorders by normative modeling
item.description: This study establishes age-specific reference ranges for hippocampal subfields and shows that personalized deviations from these norms can distinguish neurological disorders and help assess cognition and disease progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Combing-triggered electrostimulation synchronizing deep delivery for rapid hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia
item.description: Here authors introduce a comb‑shaped bioelectronic device that uses enhanced electric fields for electrostimulation and deep acid delivery for androgenetic alopecia treatment. In mouse models, they show that this safe, non‑invasive approach achieves nearly 100% hair regrowth within one month.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vivo ultrasound–MRI 3D mapping of neuromuscular compartments reveals the neuromechanical architecture of finger-specific control
item.description: Finger-specific motor control depends on neuromuscular compartments whose architecture has remained unresolved. Here, the authors combine dynamic ultrasound and MRI to map the compartments in 3D, reconstruct fibre level architecture, and validate them with anatomy and electromyography.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders
item.description: Autoimmunity has long been hypothesized in schizophrenia spectrum disorders, but antibodies diagnostic of autoimmune encephalitis are uncommon. Here, the authors show that multi-platform profiling detects rare anti-neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins
item.description: Tuunanen et al. demonstrate a vasomechanic intervention to increase the efflux of soluble human brain proteins, including Aβ, into venous sinuses. The study shows how standard neuroimaging can monitor brain fluid dynamics during preventive efforts targeting proteinopathies such as Alzheimer’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis prevents pro-metastatic niche formation through metabolic rewiring of inflammatory monocytes
item.description: Targeting the IRE1α–XBP1s stress-sensor axis is widely viewed as a promising anti-tumor strategy. Here, the authors uncover an unexpected hepatocyte-specific role for this pathway in suppressing liver metastasis through metabolic regulation of inflammatory monocytes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
item.description: The study introduces a framework for measuring fairness in epidemic models. Tested across different epidemic scenarios, it shows that fairness-aware vaccination strategies can improve health equity and overall effectiveness.

item.title: Nature Communications: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
item.description: The authors sequence 1020 Chinese patients with beta thalassemia and 409 unaffected parents to identify genes that modulate the phenotypes. Functional validation in mice and cultured cells confirm the role of autophagy-associated gene PIK3C3.

item.title: Nature Communications: MELK drives neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis via vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic transition
item.description: The study identifies MELK as a driver of harmful vascular remodeling and shows that MELK inhibition reduces neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis in mice while preserving endothelial repair, highlighting MELK as a potential treatment target.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-anchored foundation model embeddings improve molecular prediction from histology images
item.description: Obtaining accurate molecular insights for precision oncology remains costly and time consuming. Here, the authors develop PathLUPI, a deep learning method to enable effective molecular prediction in cancer using only routine whole-slide images, with evaluation across 49 molecular oncology tasks in 20 different cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Culture-independent strain typing of Clostridioides difficile in fecal samples
item.description: Here, the authors optimize MetaPhlAn4 and StrainPhlAn, to distinguish C. difficile strains in complex fecal microbiomes of hospitalized patients, showcasing the utility of metagenomic short-read sequencing for culture-independent, rapid epidemiologic surveillance of CDI in healthcare environments.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metabolic reprogramming modulates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy via GLS1 in chronic kidney disease in male mice
item.description: Chronic kidney disease often causes heart enlargement, a serious complication whose mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that excess phosphate activates the metabolic enzyme GLS1, promoting heart enlargement, while blocking GLS1 protects against this effect in male mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Excess type I interferon disrupts developmental crosstalk and promotes premature distalization in trisomy 21 lungs
item.description: Congenital lung anomalies are associated with Trisomy 21 lungs. Here, authors show that hyperactivation of the type I IFN signaling pathway promotes precocious epithelial cell differentiation, contributing to the T21 related lung pathologies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Shared genetic architecture across fibrotic diseases
item.description: The authors map the genetic architecture of 18 fibrosis-related conditions and find that fibrosis affecting anatomically distant parts shares genetic similarities, particularly in pathways involved in tissue remodeling, immune regulation and development.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reversal of trauma-induced monocyte paralysis by IFN-γ fails to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia, implicating lymphoid deficits in infection risk
item.description: The authors show that IFN-γ therapy improved monocyte HLA-DR expression in critically ill patients but failed to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia in the PREV-HAP trial. Pre-existing T- and B cell deficits, rather than monocyte status, predicted infection risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: One Health genomic surveillance identifies potential genetic links of antimicrobial-resistant foodborne pathogens across sectors
item.description: In this study, the authors use nationwide genomic data collected across sectors in Japan to identify closely related antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella and Campylobacter isolates in food and humans, highlighting the value of integrated One Health surveillance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Performance of artificial intelligence-assisted cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus testing for cervical cancer screening
item.description: The authors prove AI-assisted cytology effective for cervical cancer screening. When combined with HPV testing, it detects more precancerous lesions and maintains low referral rates.

item.title: Nature Communications: B7-H4‒directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors: the Phase 1/2a (BLUESTAR), first-in-human study
item.description: B7-H4 is a promising therapeutic target in solid tumors because of its frequent expression in cancer cells, limited normal tissue distribution, and immunosuppressive functions. In this first-in-human trial, the authors report safety and efficacy outcomes for B7-H4–directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with heavily pretreated ovarian, endometrial, and breast cancers, and cholangiocarcinoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Programmable hydrogel-nanocapsule protein delivery system targeting dense cartilage regeneration for osteoarthritis therapy
item.description: In osteoarthritis, protein therapeutics show poor joint retention and cartilage penetration. Here, authors develop a programmable two-stage, enzyme-responsive hydrogel-nanocapsule system to deliver a model protein drug and promote cartilage regeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Recruitment of TEX15 by HUSH2 drives repression of multicopy gene families in fertility regulation
item.description: In this study, Yang et al showed that the TEX15-HUSH2 complex represses multicopy gene families in haploid spermatids. Their study revealed a molecular mechanism underlying postmeiotic repression of sex chromatin (PMSC) critical for male fertility.

item.title: Nature Communications: A motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification
item.description: Early detection of scoliosis is critical for timely intervention, but current screening lacks accuracy. Here the authors develop a motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for accurate, intelligent scoliosis identification.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genomic surveillance meets clinical practice: rule-based individualized treatment prediction for gonorrhoea using SensiTyper
item.description: Golparian et al. designed and validated (13,701 global gonococcal genomes) SensiTyper, a rule-based framework predicting antimicrobial susceptibility from whole-genome sequencing data and susceptibility-guided individualized gonorrhoea treatment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tree shrew more closely recapitulates primate spermatogenesis than the mouse in cross-species single-cell transcriptomic analyses
item.description: By comparing testis cell development across four mammals, this study shows that tree shrews more closely resemble primates than mice in key stages of sperm formation, supporting their use as a complementary model of human male fertility.

item.title: Nature Communications: The accuracy-safety trade-off of large reasoning models in clinical diagnostics
item.description: This study finds that reasoning-enabled AI models improve diagnostic accuracy but produce more false positives and less consistent outputs but physician oversight helps retain benefits while reducing safety risks.
